system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

When will the data from AIM-HIGH be available? Where can I get more information on AIM-HIGH? Where can I learn more about ways to treat or prevent high cholesterol? 1. What was the purpose of the AIM-HIGH study and what questions did it plan to answer? AIM-HIGH was meant to test whether adding high dose, extended-release niacin to a statin (simvastatin) is better than a statin alone in reducing long-term cardiovascular events in participants whose LDL or “bad” cholesterol was controlled and who had a history of cardiovascular disease, low levels of HDL or “good” cholesterol, and high levels of triglycerides, another type of fat in the blood. The study examined whether the combination statin/niacin therapy was safe and whether it lowered the risk of total heart 
...
or vascular events including: coronary heart disease death, non-fatal heart attack, ischemic stroke (when arteries leading to the brain are blocked), hospital stays for acute coronary syndrome (a series of conditions affecting coronary arteries), and coronary or cerebral revascularizations (procedures to improve blood flow in the vessels of the heart or brain). 2. Researchers enrolled 3,414 volunteers. Men and women had to be at least 45 years of age with established vascular disease and dyslipidemia (too much fat in the blood) to be enrolled in AIM-HIGH. "Established vascular disease" was defined as documented by the existence of any one of the following: multi-vascular coronary artery disease , history of myocardial infarction (heart attack) , hospitalization for unstable angina (chest pain) with evidence of ischemia, ischemic stroke or peripheral artery disease . The simvastatin dose was adjusted to keep LDL levels within a target range of 40-80 mg/dL (1.0-2.1 mmol/L). The actual average follow-up is 32 months. 3. The AIM-HIGH study was conducted to find out if a treatment to raise low HDL would reduce the risk of people with this profile. 4. What did the preliminary results of the study show? AIM-HIGH data showed that, if the trial had continued, there was less than a 1 in 10,000 chance that it would ever show a significant benefit on the primary outcome measure: a reduction in the combined rates of cardiovascular disease deaths, non-fatal heart attacks, stroke due to blockage of arteries leading to the brain, hospitalization for acute coronary syndrome, or symptom driven coronary or cerebral revascularization surgeries. High dose niacin (1,000 mg to 2,000 mg or 1 to 2 grams) decreases triglyceride levels by 15 to 20 percent and increases HDL cholesterol levels by 15 to 30 percent. Reductions in LDL cholesterol are modest (less than 10 percent). 9.
